then.text: Roll up! Cambridge Science Fair. Light the right lamps, crack the code or zip up the DNA. One go a day, and a prize for a solve.
Lovely work. Have a flask of tea, scientist's fuel.

else.text: That's your go for today. The lamps need a rest, and so does the volunteer.

then.text: There goes my champion! Every punt on the Cam doffs its pole to you. Well, nods. They're busy.
You beat him? You beat Rupert? Up the Cam! Proper Cambridge style, standing on the till like a civilised person.
Here, have my lucky pole-tip. Cut from an ash tree on the Backs. Brook creatures swear by it.
You've got the pole! Rupert's waiting on the Backs, the far side of the Mathematical Bridge. Off you go, and don't let him splash you.
You'll need a proper pole. The porter at Queens' College keeps a spare, just through their door by the wooden bridge.

else.text: Afternoon! Punt tour? Ninety minutes, the Backs, King's, the Bridge of Sighs, and I'll tell you which colleges have the best ghosts.
Unless... You look sporty. Some Oxford chap called Rupert has challenged every punter on the Cam to a race, and none of my lot will take him on. They're all scared of the swan.
Race Rupert for the honour of the Cam?

then.text: Champion! First you'll need a pole. The porter at Queens' College, by the Mathematical Bridge, keeps a spare. Tell him I sent you.
We shan't speak of the race. I've already told Oxford it was foggy. It was, a bit, in my soul.
Rupert's punt drifts gently into the reeds. Back to the Punt Captain at Quayside with the news!

else.text: Rupert, Oxford. I'm racing Cambridge's best, if they ever find a pole. Ha!

then.text: The tree's grand. Somebody's grafted a bit of it for a school in Lincolnshire. It'll be falling on children's heads in no time.
He watched it fall, he didn't get bonked! I'll make a gardener of you yet. Facts are like apples: best picked carefully.
Keep the apple. And take these, for your trouble. The Trinity orchard does a fine pippin.
Show the apple to the librarian in the Wren Library, through the college gate. Then go and set that student by the Corpus Clock straight.

else.text: See this tree? Grown from the very tree in Isaac Newton's garden at Woolsthorpe. In 1666 he watched an apple drop and wondered why it always falls straight down and never sideways or up.
One's just dropped, look. There's a student over by the Corpus Clock telling everyone it hit Newton on the head. It's driving me up the wall.
Take the apple and set the story straight?

then.text: Good. Show it to the librarian in the Wren Library first, through the Trinity gate. She knows Newton better than his mother did.

else.text: Suit yourself. Apples don't wait, mind. Gravity sees to that.

then.text: I've changed all my notes. Newton watched it fall. I still think a little bonk would have been funnier.
Is that one of Newton's apples? Brilliant. You know it fell on his head, right? Boing! And then he invented gravity.
What really happened?
options: He watched one fall in his garden

then.text: Watched it fall. In his garden in Lincolnshire. He told his friend Stukeley himself. Huh. And he didn't invent gravity, he explained it. Fine. FINE.
Back to the College Gardener by the apple tree to tell him!

else.text: Hmm. Are you sure? That's not what the librarian at the Wren would say, is it? Have another think.
Did you know the Chronophage up there eats time? I've got an essay due. It's been eating mine all week.

cam_guide.text: {greeting} This street is King's Parade. Everything you can see is older than your country's motorways and better at being photographed.
Cambridge University was started in 1209 by scholars running away from Oxford after a fight with the townsfolk. The town and the gown have been rubbing along ever since.

rail_guard.text: Cambridge Station. Famously a very long way from the middle of town, because the colleges didn't want students nipping off to London.
All aboard! The trains go everywhere you have been. Mind the gap, and the bicycles.

cam_cyclist1.text: Ding! Sorry! Ding! Sorry! That's the Cambridge greeting, mate.

cam_cyclist2.text: Lost my bike outside the library. There were four thousand other bikes. One of them was probably mine.

cam_marketeer.text: Fresh strawberries, local asparagus, and a fen celery you won't find in London. The black soil up in the Fens grows the best veg in England, they say. They say it in the Fens, mostly.

cam_cowherd.text: These are proper common lands. Folk have had the right to graze cattle here for centuries. We still do. The cows have right of way too, and unlike the cyclists, they know it.

cam_bunlover.text: Fitzbillies on Trumpington Street has been selling Chelsea buns since 1920. Sticky, spiced, swirled with sugar syrup. I've had three today. It's eleven o'clock.
Chelsea buns are from London, technically. Don't tell anyone in that queue.
